A man climbed into a tiger enclosure at a wildlife park in England. Moments later, the tiger attacked him — and he never made it out alive. The incident happened on October 10, 2026, at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster, England. Authorities have identified the victim as William Chapman, a man in his early 20s who was visiting the park alone. According to South Yorkshire Police, emergency services were called shortly after 1:30 p.m. after reports that a man had entered the tiger enclosure. Inside was a five-year-old Siberian tiger named Altai. Witnesses described seeing the man approach the animal while other visitors shouted warnings. Reports say some people tried to get him to stay away from the tiger. But he entered the enclosure. The tiger attacked, leaving the man with fatal injuries. Emergency responders rushed to the scene, but he was pronounced dead at the park. Video of the incident has since circulated online. Authorities have urged people not to share the distressing footage out of respect for the victim and his family. Investigators are still examining the circumstances surrounding the incident. And there's another detail people have been asking about: what happened to the tiger? The wildlife park confirmed that Altai was unharmed and **will not be euthanized**. The park was temporarily closed following the incident while authorities carried out their investigation. This is a tragic reminder that even animals raised in managed environments remain powerful wild predators. A barrier separating visitors from an animal is there for a reason, and entering an enclosure can have irreversible consequences. William Chapman’s family is now grieving his death, and officials are asking the public to respect their privacy. What do you think should happen when a visitor deliberately enters a dangerous animal's enclosure?
